summary: E-Documents in Business Central covers setting up the E-Documents app and services, connecting to external access points and Microsoft 365, and using e-documents in sales and purchasing. It answers questions about setup, connectors, Peppol formats, status tracking, matching incoming documents, and extending the framework.
overview:
The E-Documents app manages electronic invoices and other business documents in Business Central. It supports localizations for several countries and has extension points for specific requirements. Start with the overview page, then read "Set Up E-documents". That page covers the E-Documents Service, document sending profiles, the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format, and the clearance model used in countries such as Spain, India, Mexico, and Italy.

Three pages cover connections. One explains connecting to external access points (Pagero, Avalara, Logiq, ExFlow, B2BRouter). Another covers installing the E-Document Core app and connector apps from Microsoft Marketplace, then configuring services, GLN, customers, and workflows for non-Microsoft endpoints. A third covers connecting Outlook, SharePoint, and OneDrive to import vendor invoices and receipts.

For daily work, "Use e-documents in sales" covers creating and sending e-invoices and credit memos, sending them as email attachments, and checking status and logs. "Use E-Documents in the purchase process" covers receiving, matching, vendor setup, and error handling. Developers building localizations or ISV extensions should read "Extending the e-documents functionality".
key_points: The E-Documents app manages sales and purchase e-documents, tracks document status, and supports Peppol formats.

Setup covers the E-Documents Service, document sending profiles, data exchange, and automatic import and processing. A clearance model is described for countries such as Spain, India, Mexico, and Italy.
The listed connectors to external access points are Pagero, Avalara, Logiq, ExFlow, and B2BRouter, and they use OAuth 2.0 authentication.
Connecting to non-Microsoft endpoints requires the E-Document Core app and connector apps from Microsoft Marketplace, plus setup of GLN, customer e-documents, and workflows.
Microsoft 365 connectors (Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive) import vendor invoices and receipts for accounts payable, using E-Document Services and Service Integration V2.
In sales you can create and send e-invoices and credit memos in Peppol formats, view status and logs, and send documents as email attachments.
Purchasing supports invoices, orders, and credit memos, with automatic matching, purchase order matching with Copilot, text-to-account mapping, and item reference mapping.
The extension framework covers document format creation, service integration, async sending, batch processing, response handling, and document receiving. The page references 2025 release wave 1.

issues: Overview says "Transmission needs a connector." The sources don't say that, and the sales page lists sending e-documents as email attachments. Reworded so connectors are presented as the way to reach access points, not a requirement for every transmission.
Key point 2 says the clearance model "applies to Spain, India, Mexico, and Italy", which reads as a complete list. The source says "countries like" these, so it's now worded as examples.

Key point 8 attaches "2025 release wave 1" to the whole extension framework. The source only lists it as a version reference on the page. Reworded to say the page references that release instead of tying every feature to it.
Minor: Copilot mapping from the overview page and version 24.0 from the setup page are left out. Both omissions are acceptable.
